candidates.tagline: Nike World Cup jerseys gave every player cartoon shoulder pads — official fix: iron them
candidates.story: Nike's 2026 World Cup match kits for France, Brazil, England, USA and others have a structural seam defect that makes the shoulder panels protrude stiffly outward; the internet dubbed it 'Shredder Shoulders,' and Nike's official workaround for a jersey worn in live World Cup matches is to steam or iron it flat.
candidates.why_funny: A $1B sportswear company spent years on 'computational design' for the biggest sporting event on Earth, produced jerseys that make elite athletes look like TMNT villains, and told fans to get an iron.
candidates.alt: Close-up comparison of Nike 2026 World Cup jersey shoulders showing the stiff protruding seam flaw nicknamed Shredder Shoulders, where the shoulder panels jut out at a pointed angle instead of lying flat

candidates.tagline: Sony's AI camera 'enhancement' made photos objectively worse — proven by Sony's own ad
candidates.story: Sony launched an AI Camera Assistant for the Xperia 1 VIII that supposedly improves your photos, then posted official before/after marketing shots where the AI-processed version was visibly washed out, overexposed and lower quality; Nothing CEO Carl Pei publicly asked 'This must be engagement farming?' and Sony had to quietly post new comparisons.
candidates.why_funny: Sony ran a marketing campaign to prove their AI made photos better, accidentally proved the opposite, and had to reshoot their own proof.
candidates.alt: Side-by-side before/after comparison of photos processed by Sony Xperia AI Camera Assistant, showing the AI-enhanced right panel is noticeably washed out with reduced colour and contrast compared to the original
